fixes.explanation: That's what Moses says, baker: “But you who held fast to the LORD your God are alive to this day, every one of you.” Not most of you. Not the lucky ones. EVERY one. Right before that, he says the LORD destroyed all who followed Baal of Peor, a false god (Deuteronomy 4:3). Two groups, two outcomes, and the ones holding on to the LORD are standing there listening.

Yes, friend. Moses says the LORD brought them out of Egypt, the iron furnace, “…to be the people of His inheritance, as you are today.” A furnace is a hot, hard place to be stuck. I know a little about being stuck in a tight spot, and I only got out of mine because somebody came and got me. The LORD didn't just open the door for Israel. He took them as His own.

Freedom is a nice guess, but it isn't the reason Moses gives. He says the statutes and ordinances are so Israel “…may live and may enter and take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving you.” Notice who's doing the giving. It's the LORD, not Israel earning anything. Nobody's working a punch card here.

Hidden is a fair guess, but it isn't Moses' word. He asks what nation has a god “…as near to them as the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on Him?” I think Moses sounds amazed by how close the LORD is. Hidden is the opposite of that. Near is the word, and it's a good one.

Tribes is a good Israel word, but it's not the one on these tablets. Moses says the LORD declared His covenant, “…the Ten Commandments that He wrote on two tablets of stone.” Twelve tribes and ten commandments, so I get why the numbers got tangled. I'd mix up my own mustache tricks before I'd mix those up twice. Commandments is what fills the blank.

Right, friend. Moses says that if they act corruptly and make an idol, “You will not live long upon it, but will be utterly destroyed.” Before he says it, he calls heaven and earth as witnesses (Deuteronomy 4:26). It's a heavy warning, and I think Moses means for it to be taken seriously.
